Imo, the negative side had three focal points:

* **Scriptwriting**. I've neither read the books nor delved deep in lore, but it was obvious that in the last seasons the writing was declining for whatever reasons. This is not just on the writers however, they didn't suddenly become incompetent. The way the story developed, whilst it was brilliant to follow, it also made the future story tougher and tougher. I'm convinced this is a key reason why the original author has struggled mightily to continue the story. If the original author with much better writing credentials and practically infinite time has (almost) failed, then no wonder the tv writers struggled and the show's writing quality dropped.

* **Acting**. The casting of the older characters was near perfect throughout the series. The concept of the older generation getting slowly eclipsed by younger characters is ingenious and poses little to no challenge in book format. In video format however, it's an extremely precarious one as you practically have to hire young inexperienced actors in a longterm project which has all kinds of drawbacks, the most important of which is acting ability and suitability for the characters' transformations. By the latter I mean that a child/young actor can initially be suitable for his role but as the story develops, the character changes and this transformation may not follow that of the young actor's. So in the show, while the initial children/young casting was fine,  as the show progressed, the adult reliable actors' time was continuously decreasing and the youth had to carry the show. That was always going to be a dice-roll and as is always the case when luck is involved, results varied. Opinions differ but way I saw it, in short, Daenerys-Jon Snow were ok to decent in acting, Sansa-Arya-Bran-Sam below average, Theon-Joffrey good to very good. Thus, transitioning from an acting level of 8-9/10 to 6-7/10 is a major issue and that's unfixable no matter how popular the show becomes; in fact the influx of attention and money for young actors often works negatively as they're not used to the pressure and with the sudden massive salaries their motivation may wane.

* **HBO business model**. The show was grandiose from the start but in the early seasons they could avoid very demanding scenes (both money and time wise) by skipping/shortening battles as expectations were lower and there was the excuse of the most important battles happening in later seasons. In the final seasons however, that excuse was gone and expectations were massive, viewers wanted blockbuster level of action and visuals in a tv show format. That's ridiculous as that kind of money and time can't go in a tv show, at least in this day and age. What would the network gain by spending like 2-3 years for a season and multiple hundreds of millions more ? They'd get better reviews but their income would remain roughly the same whilst having put in a lot more effort and money. The return of investment wasn't there, hence why I believe the tv show business model was at fault, even the network's where they push the limitations further than anyone. In order for the fans to have gotten the grand finale they wanted while simultaneously making sense for the network to put a lot more into it, it needed to end in cinema as a film, or even two films Avengers style. Take extra time to be more comfortable in all regards and put in huge 200mil film budgets in a guaranteed investment as everyone would be paying tickets to watch it.

There is some truth in that but it's not absolute. For example, you can be honest-intelligent-supportive of an authoritarian regime if you consider it better than the alternative/previous regime. Finally, authoritarian/totalitarian are 20th century terms but their core is close to autocracy which has been around since pre-history and there have been capable autocrats that someone honest-intelligent could have supported.
